overview: Mauritania became independent from France on 28 November 1960. This modern republic must be distinguished from ancient Mauretania farther north. Its desert towns and teaching traditions are much older than the state, while the 1960 atlas outline represents modern territorial coverage rather than the birth of those communities.

periods.title: Independence and changing governments
periods.summary: The republic’s international independence dates to November 1960.

periods.title: An elected transfer and continuing challenges
periods.summary: In 2019 power passed between elected presidents for the first time.

sections.title: A modern republic with older places

items.text: Independence in 1960 followed French rule. The diplomatic record identifies 28 November as the decisive date and names Moktar Ould Daddah as prime minister at recognition. The republic joined an international system of states, but its residents’ connections across desert, river and coast long predated that event.

The older towns of Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt and Oualata served trans-Saharan caravan routes. Their surviving fabric developed over medieval centuries, not after independence. Courtyard houses cluster along twisting lanes near mosques with square minarets, preserving the physical arrangement of communities built around travel, trade and religious learning.

The ksour also contained warehouses for protecting goods. Dense building patterns, blank outer walls and internal courtyards show how household space and storage fitted a desert setting. UNESCO identifies sand movement and changing construction methods as conservation problems: keeping an old town alive requires care for ordinary houses as well as celebrated monuments.

A mahadra classroom can be a tent with mats, carpets and cushions on the ground. In the tradition described by UNESCO in 2023, listening and memorizing connect students with teachers and with one another. Religion, language and literature share the learning space; a permanent school building is not the only setting for serious study.

Mahadra learning also includes reading animal tracks, recognizing medicinal plants and using stars to find direction. Poetry and storytelling pass through the same community networks. These descriptions record kinds of knowledge people teach, rather than establishing the effectiveness of every historical remedy.

The official Arabic constitution prints the motto “شرف،إخاء، عدل”: “Honor, Fraternity, Justice.” This sample is from article 9 of the 1991 constitution as revised, in the Constitutional Council’s online text. Article 6 recognizes Arabic, Pulaar, Soninke and Wolof as national languages, showing that one Arabic quotation cannot represent every Mauritanian voice.

At Banc d’Arguin, Imraguen fishers work on foot with nets and from sailing boats called lanches. The park authority describes lateen sails and a prohibition on motorboats within the protected fishery. Knowing the shallow water, wind and fish movements matters as much as owning a boat.

Fishing households’ work continues after a catch comes ashore. The park’s 2010 to 2014 management plan records support for women processing and marketing poutargue, a preserved fish-roe product, and transport for village cooperatives. Food preparation, preservation and selling were part of the economy, not a footnote to the fishermen’s work.

UNICEF’s energy case study describes manually drilled boreholes combined with solar pumps, storage reservoirs and small distribution networks. Five drilling stations with solar pumping were supported in 2020 and 2021, alongside training for local operators. A pump needs someone who can maintain it after the installation team has left.

A photograph in the same report shows a woman cleaning a solar panel serving a cooperative’s market garden. The caption explains that pumped water supports crops, income and fruit and vegetables for children. In this setting, cleaning a panel is part of the work that helps dinner grow.

Legal reform did not immediately end inherited forms of exploitation. In 2018 the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child welcomed stronger anti-slavery law but reported continuing caste-based slavery affecting children. It called for investigations, freedom, family support and access to school. The concern was people’s lived freedom, beyond words in legislation.

The 2019 transfer from one elected president to another was a political milestone identified by the UN Peacebuilding Commission. It did not mean that the state began again or that all social problems were solved. Mauritania’s history continues through institutions, local learning and the daily work of its diverse communities.

ending.text: Mauritania remains a continuing republic whose independence dates to 1960. Changes of leadership are distinct from the survival of its communities and from the much older desert towns they preserve.
